primitives.name: Surrender API
primitives.desc: Wallet-driven surrender flow: CIP-30 partial-sign, a co-signer that signs only after the claimant has and whose witness the primary verifies before it signs, re-verifying every transaction against a strict surrender policy (golden-tested on every mainnet surrender) that refuses any input, collateral, collateral return or output naming a credential on the deny-list (both signers, each on its own; the API also answers such an address 403 before any build, and neither starts without the list), its own chain view (every input unspent on chain, no unit above its pinned supply, no pinned NFT minted or burned since the pin, and of each surrendered unit, what is surrendered held under the claimant's payment key for the 72 hours before, with every unit that arrived from another key or was minted since counted against the holding, followed back through the claimant's own transfers and through the inputs of any surrender the signer recorded whose change it rides in, asking about each transaction once and refusing past 256 lookups, so no ancestry costs a check more; the builder spends the units held longest first, asking where at most 256 of the claimant's holders were made) and a per-signer ledger that refuses approvals that can never land and holds each legacy unit to its pinned remaining supply, each merge asset to the supply the rate table funded the pool for (T2_ADAM_PASS: 95 editions, not the 150 on chain), and the pool to a 24-hour cap, a pin check against the chain tip that reads supply and NFT history as the signers do and confirms any record of waived units in quarantine against the transaction that sent them and the waived reserve, a page to the on-call Discord channel for every surrender either signer is about to sign and every refusal under a deny rule (written to an outbox before the signature, delivered only once Discord returns a message id, retried across restarts; neither signer starts without it), pool-tip tracking, an answer telling a wallet that cannot fund a surrender how much ADA or collateral it needs (wallet_needs_ada / wallet_needs_collateral), and UTxO defrag tooling. Shared chain-provider configuration preserves network-specific Blockfrost defaults, supports opt-in network-checked Insight URLs and service-owned 0400/0600 file credentials, and gives service environment precedence over dotenv.

primitives.name: Compromised-credential deny-list
primitives.desc: One JSON list of compromised Cardano payment and stake key or script hashes, each with its on-chain evidence, and the rescue credentials it must never deny; a strict loader (refuses any other shape, a repeated key or hash, a hash both denied and allowed, an empty list) with a JSON Schema beside the data for consumers in other languages, and an address check that denies an address naming a listed credential in either part and refuses pointer and unreadable addresses. v1 lists the 10-30 drain: the attacker's two addresses, W1, W2, the drained decimalist accounts and other victims, their liquidity-contract and timelock scripts, the burned wallets, and the waived treasury reserves.
